Crispy Smashed Potatoes

Golden, crispy edges with creamy centers. These smashed potatoes are the perfect side dish that looks impressive but couldn't be easier to make.

NickHome Cook & Writer
Jump to Recipe
Prep 10 min
Cook 45 min
Total 55 min
Servings 4

If there’s one side dish that’s earned a permanent spot in my weeknight rotation, it’s these crispy smashed potatoes. They’re the kind of recipe that makes people ask for seconds and assume you spent way more time in the kitchen than you actually did.

Why This Recipe Works

The magic of smashed potatoes is in the technique. By boiling them first, you get that creamy, fluffy interior. Then smashing and roasting at high heat creates all those irresistible crispy edges and golden bits. It’s the best of both worlds.

I’ve been making these for years, tweaking the recipe each time. The version you see here is the result of testing different potato varieties, oven temperatures, and herb combinations. Trust me when I say: this is the one.

The Secret to Extra Crispy Edges

The crispiest smashed potatoes come down to three things:

  1. Dry potatoes: After boiling, let them sit for a few minutes before smashing. The drier the surface, the crispier they’ll get.

  2. Hot oil on the pan: Drizzle oil on the baking sheet before adding the potatoes. This creates a frying effect on the bottom.

  3. Don’t crowd them: Give each potato room to breathe. Crowded potatoes steam instead of crisp.

Make It Your Own

This basic recipe is endlessly adaptable. Here are some variations I love:

  • Parmesan version: Add 1/4 cup grated Parmesan in the last 5 minutes of roasting
  • Spicy kick: Add red pepper flakes with the herbs
  • Loaded style: Top with sour cream, chives, and crumbled bacon
  • Mediterranean: Use oregano instead of rosemary and top with crumbled feta

Crispy Smashed Potatoes

Golden, crispy edges with creamy centers. These smashed potatoes are the perfect side dish that looks impressive but couldn't be easier to make.

Servings:
4
servings

Ingredients

For the potatoes

  • 2 lbs baby potatoes (Yukon Gold or red potatoes)
  • 4 tbsp olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic (minced)
  • 2 tbsp fresh rosemary (chopped)
  • 1 tbsp fresh thyme (leaves only)
  • 1 tsp kosher salt
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish)

For serving

  • flaky sea salt (to taste)

Instructions

  1. 1

    Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water by 2 inches. Add 1 tablespoon of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook until fork-tender, about 20-25 minutes.

  2. 2

    Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper and drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil.

  3. 3

    Drain the potatoes and let them cool for 5 minutes. Arrange them on the prepared baking sheet, leaving space between each potato.

  4. 4

    Using the bottom of a glass or a potato masher, gently press down on each potato until it's about 1/2 inch thick. Some will break apart—that's fine and creates extra crispy bits.

    Tip: Don't press too hard—you want them flattened but not completely mashed.

  5. 5

    Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the potatoes. Sprinkle with minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.

  6. 6

    Roast for 25-30 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until the edges are deeply golden and crispy.

  7. 7

    Remove from oven, sprinkle with flaky sea salt and fresh parsley, and serve immediately.

Notes

These are best served right out of the oven when they're at their crispiest. If you need to make them ahead, you can boil and smash the potatoes earlier in the day, then roast them just before serving.

Testing Notes

We tested this recipe with both Yukon Gold and red potatoes. Both work great, but Yukon Golds get slightly crispier edges. We also tried using a wire rack for extra crispness, but found the parchment paper method produced nearly identical results with less cleanup.

Chef's Tip from Xavier

For restaurant-level crispy potatoes, try the double-fry method: after smashing, refrigerate uncovered for an hour to dry out the surface, then roast. The drier surface means crispier results.

Nutrition (per serving)

Calories 245
Protein 4g
Carbs 28g
Fat 14g
